Once the yogi Narada, wishing to help others, sees the sufferings of people in the Kali age and asks how their sorrow may surely end. He goes to the white, four-armed Narayana, who is calm, cheerful and praised by Sanaka and others. Narada says that duty has four feet with truth as its ornament, and the best means is the Satya Narayana vow, and asks what the fruit and rule are. The Lord says that by it a person bound is freed, a fearful one becomes fearless. One bathes in the morning, is pure, takes a tooth-stick, resolves "I will keep your vow", and worships in the evening, with Shaligrama and gold, and recites the six-chapter story. The offering is divided between the teacher and the family, and Brahmins are fed. Narada then goes to heaven.

06-025.json.summary: Suta tells of the famous city of Kashi and an excellent but poor Brahmin there. Narayana appears to a gentle, humble man and says "by my advice, worship Satya Narayana". The Brahmin, instructed by the kind Hari, praises him with a hymn, describing him in a yellow garment with lotus eyes. The Lord gives the rule: with little effort and simple faith one worships, offering wheat flour with ghee, Ganga water with honey and the five nectars, with sweet food, drink, fruit and honour, surrounded by Brahmins and relatives, and the offering is eaten with respect. The Lord vanishes. The Brahmin and his wife do as told, call relatives and friends, and the Brahmin asks for happiness here and hereafter. He receives a chariot, an elephant, a house and a horse. They bow to the ground and receive the offering, and he spreads the worship of Satya Narayana in the world.

06-026.json.summary: Suta tells of a calm, gentle, wise king devoted to Narayana, Chandrachuda of Manipura, who fights a dreadful battle with proud foreigners. His great army goes to Yama's city, and five thousand footmen die and go to heaven. Overcome by the foreigners, he goes to Kashi on the pretext of a pilgrimage. He sees the city rich in wealth and grain, is amazed, and, seeing the Brahmin Sadananda who worships the true god, bows to him. Sadananda describes the Satya Narayana vow: gateways and plantain pillars, a lovely altar built by Brahmins in the middle, and worship with perfumes and flowers with love and devotion. The king worships in Kashi, takes a sword that destroys the enemy's side, kills six thousand bandits, and gains great wealth. By keeping the vow on every full-moon day, he becomes lord of a hundred thousand villages.

06-027.json.summary: Suta tells that some hunters go to Kashi to sell wood from the forest. They see Hari, served by Brahmins, and a Brahmin once seen as poor now seen as very rich, and ask how he got his wealth. Sadananda tells them of the Satya Narayana worship and the history of how a Nishada came to his hermitage. The rule is: wheat flour with ghee, bathing the god with the five nectars, and worship with sandal and others with fruit, flowers, incense and lamps. Pure devotion pleases him more than many things. He left the honour offered by Duryodhana, and ate the rice grains of Sudama. A cowherd, a vulture, a merchant, a hunter, Hanuman and Vibhishana reached him and are happy still. The hunters sell the wood, worship with the proceeds, bow at the end of the story and take the offering. By the power of the worship they gain children and wives and enjoy pleasures, and the poor and blind are said to gain as they wish.

06-028.json.summary: Suta tells of King Chandrachuda of Manipura and, in the city of Ratnapura, a merchant (Sadhu) who owns a hundred thousand. He sees many people at a river shore, rests his boat to see the wonder, and asks what they are doing. They say the worship of the true god gives wealth, a son, and all wishes. He wishes for a child, goes home thinking of Hari, holds festivals, and then has a lotus-eyed daughter. A daughter is said to be ten years old before she is a young woman. He chooses a fitting groom and gives the daughter with Vedic sound and music. He treats his son-in-law like a son. He then leaves with ships on trade. While all sleep, thieves steal his great wealth. The king hears of the theft, is angry, and has the merchant and son-in-law arrested and chained for twelve months, as the god was hostile. They lament.

06-029.json.summary: Suta continues the merchant's story. When Hari is against one, he says, many hells await. The merchant's wife Kalavati and her daughter, without food or clothing, are in need, and a man, Shilapala, gives five coins. The king is taught by a Brahmin in a dream. The merchant and his son-in-law say they are not thieves, ask to be judged truly, and the minister speaks. They are freed with song and music. Later an ascetic tells the merchant that his wealth is not in the boats, and the merchant faints from worry. The ascetic says that when King Chandrachuda worshipped Satya Narayana, he did not honour him, so how can he prosper? The merchant asks forgiveness and the pleased Narayana grants his wish. Kalavati ignores the offering and hurries away, and her son-in-law sinks with the boat; she faints, and is told to take the offering quickly. By the power of the vow the merchant is blessed with sons and grandsons. This is called the best of vows.

06-030.json.summary: The sages ask Suta about the highest celibate life, and Suta says that in the terrible Kali age, there is no forest-dwelling stage and celibacy is seen only here and there. A man asks what stage and class will do him good, and decides to take a wife, thus praising Shiva, the auspicious one, with a hymn that salutes Nature, the mother of the great principle, who makes the pairs of opposites, and Ignorance and Purity. A Brahmin marries the goddess named Brahmacharini and gives the seasonal gift to his wife. The four Vedas are named. The son of the Yajurveda is the Mimamsa teacher, and Vararuchi, a favourite of the king, is the son of the Atharva Veda. The king honours them. Vyadi, Mimamsa and Panini each speak to Chandragupta, and Vararuchi speaks to the king of Magadha. The student with staff and the almsman is named, and Pitrisharma meditates on Damodara.

06-031.json.summary: Suta tells that Panini, ashamed, goes to other holy places, drinks the water at Kedara and meditates on Shiva. After ten days he lives on air for ten days and, hearing nectar-like words, praises the god with a choking voice: "salutation to Bharga, the destroyer of sin, endless and Creator", and asks him to give the root of knowledge. The god says that the mind is the great holy place in the lake of knowledge, with the water of truth removing the dirt of passion and hatred, which shows Brahman. Then Rudra vanishes and Panini goes home. After composing the Linga-sutra, he attains the highest liberation. The Ganga herself, the auspicious one made of all holy places, comes there.

06-032.json.summary: Suta tells that Bopadeva goes to lovely Vrindavana, served by cowherds and cowherd women, and at the end of a year Hari himself gives him the best knowledge, described by Shuka to the wise Vishnurata. At the end of the story the Lord Vishnu appears. Bopadeva says people tormented by hell are fulfilled through his name in the Kali age. The Lord says the world will be ruled by Buddhists, made of pride and hypocrisy. The goddess Shiva asks who the best god is and, hearing the answer, goes to a secret place where Chandisha, Ganesha, Nandin and Guha are. The god tells her a lovely story kept in his mind. A parrot in a hollow hears it, becomes long-lived, and gains the greatness of the Bhagavata. The goddess is told to go to the bank of the Narmada and recite the story, and to give it to a worthy Vishnu devotee. Bopadeva then vanishes.

06-033.json.summary: The sages ask by which hymn one gains the fruit of reciting the Vedas, and Suta tells a story. A Brahmin named Tripathin has a wife, Kamini. He goes to recite the Saptashati for a living and stays away for a month. She meets a hunter who lives by selling wood and conceives by him. After twelve years the cunning son, who has no Vedic learning, and his mother are driven out by the Brahmin. Living on the Vindhya mountain, they recite the Chandika text daily, and both live happily in a hunter's house in the forest. The son steals, takes a woman's ornaments, and once receives something taken from a Brahmin's clothes, but by the merit of reciting the text he turns to righteousness and becomes a pupil, reciting the letters of Shiva. A worm-like being comes out of him, burnt in many colours. He recites the Adi Charita and praises Annapurna with a hymn. After a hundred and eight recitations the goddess gives him the Rigveda and disappears. He becomes the priest for King Vikramaditya's sacrifice.

06-034.json.summary: Suta tells that a wicked man out of greed for meat ate pigs and village cocks, then human flesh, and gave up everything else. The fearful man has the Chandika recitation done. He becomes a Kshatriya king of Magadha again, remembers his past lives and follows Vedic duty. A sage gives the king the middle episode of the Devi Mahatmya, and the king worships the eternal Mahalakshmi daily. By the grace of Mahamaya the place becomes holy. After twelve years his teacher, devoted to Shakti, arrives, and the eternal goddess, mother of the world, appears. The king, great and fortunate, enjoys pleasures the gods desire. Suta says this is the fate of the Yajurveda as told, and the greatness described by the sage.

06-035.json.summary: Suta tells of a man who knows the Vedas and their branches and is devoted to the Gita. Once he goes on a pilgrimage, and at the end of the year he is won over by a devotee of the goddess. Patanjali praises her: "you are faith, understanding, memory, learning, and the one who does good". A disembodied voice says he will gain true knowledge by the power of her story. He goes to the temple of Vindhyavasini and gains the knowledge that is her grace and turns to Vishnu. He wears the upright mark, tilaka and a tulasi necklace, and recites the Mahabhashya joyfully to each person. Suta says this is the best prayer to recite and ends with a blessing: may all see good and none share in sorrow. The listener who is pure and hears the collection of histories is blessed.

07-001.json.summary: This chapter begins the fourth part of the Pratisarga. The sages ask about the play the Lord performed at that time. Suta says that in the great kalpa called Bhavishya, in the Vaivasvata age, the Pandavas defeated the proud Kauravas. At the end of a day Krishna, knowing the bad turn of time, asks Shiva to protect the Pandavas who are his devotees. At night Ashvatthama, Bhoja and Kripa come, and Ashvatthama kills with a sword given by Shiva. A charioteer of Dhrishtadyumna survives, frightened. Learning that Shiva has done wrong, Bhima and the others become angry and their weapons enter Shiva's body. Rudra curses them: "you are worshippers of Krishna and will be reborn in the Kali age and bear this fault". They take refuge in Hari and praise Rudra, and Shiva appears. Krishna says he gave the curse out of necessity and tells who will be born: Yudhishthira as Vatsaraja's son, Bhima as a foreigner, a part of Arjuna as a devotee, Nakula at Kanyakubja, Sahadeva, a part of Dhritarashtra at Ajmer, and Karna as Taraka. Mahavati is a lovely city made by Mayadevi, and a part of Krishna is born as Udayasimha. He says he will kill the kings of the fire line and establish Kali.

07-002.json.summary: Suta describes kings who taught the duties of kings, liberation and giving, and went to heaven after ruling thirty-six years. Vyasa says the sages of Naimisha, after twelve hundred years, rise at a divine pool and do bathing and meditation. They name the lands, from the west end of the Sindhu river to Setubandha in the south, Ajmer, Marudhanva, Avanti, Udupa, Vanga, Gauda and Magadha, where many languages and religions stand. Hearing of the ruin of duty, they come with many groups by the Himalaya and Sindhu routes. A grandson of Vikramaditya takes his father's kingdom, sets a boundary between the foreigners and Aryas, and makes a foreign settlement beyond the Sindhu. In the middle of the Huna country, a good man on a mountain tells the king that he teaches the foreigners' way, and that a fearful being called Ishamasi appeared among bandits at the decline of truth. He tells the king to recite a pure Vedic prayer and meditate on the Lord in the sun's disc. The king bows, regains his kingdom and performs a horse sacrifice.

07-003.json.summary: Suta tells that the limits of duty were slowly lost on earth. A king with ten thousand soldiers and Kalidasa conquers the foreigners of Gandhara, Kashmir and Narava. Another foreigner comes with a teacher, and King Bhoja prays to Mahadeva, "lord of Girija, dweller in the desert, hidden by foreigners, pure and of the form of being, consciousness and bliss". The land of Bahlika is polluted by foreigners, with a great magician whom the god had burnt earlier. The god tells the king not to go to the demon-like land. The king returns home. A man skilled in magic speaks to him lovingly and tells him to eat his leftovers. The king's mind turns to the foreign way. Kalidasa, angry, says he will kill the wicked Bahlika, recites ten thousand times and makes the fire offering. The frightened disciples go to Bahlika. At night a god-like man tells the king that his Aryan way is the best. He says those who are circumcised, shaveless, bearded and defile are different, and that animals should be eaten except by the Kaula rite. The king returns home and sets up the Prakrit language for Shudras and a boundary for the foreigners. People of Aryan classes stay beyond the Vindhyas, and mixed castes live in Barbara, Tushara and many islands.

07-004.json.summary: Suta says the earth had many kings in their kingdom, and three kings of their line died within two hundred years. The king ruled his own kingdom by duty at Kalpakshetra. In Indraprastha Anangapala of the Tomara family is named. The fire line grew stronger, from the north to the end of China and to Setubandha in the south, with fire-offering makers who care for cows and Brahmins. A time like the Dvapara age returns everywhere, with a god and a sacrifice in every village and land. Seeing this, the terrible Kali, afraid with Mleccha, practised meditation for twelve years. Kali praises Hari, who removes all sin and makes all time, saying he has lost his body, family and kingdom. Krishna, laughing, says a part of him will come to earth and destroy the mighty ones, and vanishes. A king keeps the nine-night Durga vow for nine years, and the goddess grants a boon. He marries by duty and settles her at home. Acharya, Vatsaraja, a foreigner called Shatayatta and the mighty Talana are named. A battle of the two kings is dreadful, and then they make friendship with Talana.

07-005.json.summary: Suta tells of the birth of two girls by Shiva's favour, for King Someshvara of the Chauhan family. A Brahmin, Jayasharma, is in trance on the Himalaya, gives up his body, and a part of Nakula is born on earth by Shiva's command. He conquers Gauda, Vanga and others and the proud desert lands. Three proud sons are born to Kirtimalini, and Simhakhela at twelve years. Dhundhukara rules at Mathura and his younger brother at Ajmer. A strong son of Pradyota named Parimala is born, and Bhishmasimha, lord of elephants, from Vidyota. Seeing those unfriendly to him, he drives them from his kingdom. A bold son who gained his maternal grandfather's kingdom is told by those he has driven out how he can enjoy all the kingdom. King Jayachandra says "Parimala, you are brave, be my minister now". They are glad. A fort city is built, and Delhi is founded at a good time at the fort's gate, and the king, amazed, names it Delhi. After three years Jayachandra asks Prithviraj why he did not give his share, and sends a messenger. A proud king says he drove out the cunning men of the moon line and gathered sixteen hundred thousand troops, and that the strong king must pay tax. Jayachandra, afraid of Prithviraj, is shown, and Prithviraj takes half the kingdom.

07-006.json.summary: Suta tells that Mahiraja (Prithviraj) is amazed at the news. A woman named Tilaka is named. A Gauda king's daughter, Divyavibhavari, has a daughter, Samyogini. At Kanyakubja a golden image of Kamakshi is set up. The goddess says to a father that if he worships this yogini she will be dear to him. Five thousand chariots with archers, Dhundhukara, lord of elephants, and eight hundred thousand horses are named. The army stretches twenty krosha. On the far bank of the Ishani river, a palanquin is placed. Pradyota and Vidyota guard Ratnabhanu. Horses die by horses and elephants by elephants. The battle lasts five days with great loss of heroes. A hundred thousand horses die and go to heaven. Dhundhukara strikes Pradyota in the heart with arrows, three spears fell him to the ground, and a spear kills him and he goes to heaven. Lakshana, with them, fights angrily. The two equal heroes fight on elephants. When the mighty one is killed, the people of Kanyakubja flee in fear of Mahiraja, to their homes. Prithviraj wins, and Jayachandra's fame in battle is told. Jayachandra rules at Kanyakubja and Prithviraj at Delhi.

07-007.json.summary: Suta tells that Bhishmasimha, on the Ganga's bank in the sign of Leo, worships Indra, and after a month Indra, knowing his devotion, gives him gifts and vanishes. At that time Parimala, grieving for his father, goes to Kashi to die with his wife. A serpent at a root tells the Rudra serpent that he is cruel and slow-witted, and he has been glad in the king's body every day. A fool king, it says, is the one who does not give hot oil. The king does what the serpent said and is freed of disease. At midnight in the darkness, a sun appears in all directions, and he praises Shiva with the Mahimna hymn. Mahadeva takes the form of a linga. Malkhana, pleased, comes to Mahavati and goes to Jayachandra's city after a year. Lakshana, a hero, prays to the lord of Usha. Within a fortnight Vishnu, the lord of the world, answers, and Lakshana goes home on the elephant Airavati. They live together in friendship. A group says they will go to their cities, and the king agrees. Karinari, Sulalita and others are named. Talana is a hero at his son's command, dear to Rakshasas, and two sons of Vasuman are named. The king is given a five-voiced great serpent from Indra and a horse, Papiha, a gift of the sun, with a human voice. The army is sixty thousand, with Talana as its lord. Protected by these heroes the king is fulfilled.

07-008.json.summary: Suta says Mahadeva, having said so, vanished. A strong man speaks to his sister, who is lovely and wants victory. After giving gifts to Brahmins, he goes to the city of Jayachandra. He goes in refuge to Rudra, Shambhu with matted hair, who is a refuge. The enemy's heroes are killed. They destroy the enemy army and cry out in victory repeatedly. The rest of the enemies come together to slay their foes. The army of Mahishmati comes out in all ten directions. After deluding all enemies, he goes to his own camp. Five months after Bhishma-simha died, a part of Sahadeva is born on earth by Shiva's command.

07-009.json.summary: Suta tells of a courtesan, Lakshavritti, skilled in song and dance. Two brave men, honoured by the king, stay there. A child shown to be a part of Rama has a cheerful face. The Brahmins name him Balakhani, "of great strength". Jambuka comes with his army, seizes the whole city, burns it and goes home. Samanta takes him to his father-in-law's house. People ask whether a sun-like form of the gods has been born, and the whole city is joyful. A part of Krishna plays with his brothers in the sandalwood forest. At the age of eight he begins rites such as the naming letters.

07-010.json.summary: Suta says that kings on the side of Jayachandra fear him. The king says many local rulers are in his land, and Balakhani is ready to wrestle with him. Lakshana speaks to the supreme king. In a moment of fighting, the king throws him to the ground. When Krishna's part is nine years old, boys like Ahlada are born, divine-bodied, adorned and able to move in sky and water. He enjoys love, and horses are born of her. A lovely maiden is given to the son Brahmananda, and all the kings, struck by her, shoot their arrows at each other. The king, seeing their valour, is glad.

07-011.json.summary: Suta tells that knowledge of time is given to a god and knowledge of Brahman to a king. A wise man bows to his maternal uncle and the others in the court. At a well he sees good women filling pots. The king, afraid, gives due offerings to his sister. Devasimha, knower of time, hears of the enemy's coming, and they come to fight with a loud noise. Vatsaja cuts down the enemy's arms and weapons with his sword. The strong Sukhakhani comes. Prithviraj, shamed by his defeat, goes home with Brahmananda.

07-012.json.summary: Suta tells of a war with cannibal foreigners and a king, with three hundred thousand horses and ten thousand camels. A woman sees a beautiful dark-limbed best of men. A man says he is Udayasimha, come to avenge his father. In the night a river of their blood flows quickly. The enemy Kaliya is bound with strong chains. They kill Vankana and Rankana with a sword. In the great forest above the Vindhya, full of many beasts, the king, deluded by divine illusion, meets two who speak kindly. They come to Mahavati, their purpose achieved.

07-013.json.summary: The sages ask. The chapter tells of gifts of cows, gold, jewels and many clothes. King Netrasimha comes with his army. He goes to the flower-garden in Mahavati, crosses Vanga, quickly reaches the Himalaya, and has a thousand elephants and a hundred thousand horses. Someone tells Udayasimha to go to the temple of Kamakshi. When the drum is stolen, Netrasimha is afraid. The text describes the Aryas and Abhiras. Krishna's part goes up against Yogasimha. A terrible battle of five hundred thousand and seven hundred thousand follows. Malana, the king, holds festivals in each house.

07-014.json.summary: Suta says that on Thursday at noon on the ninth bright day of Chaitra, Ahlada joyfully has the child's birth rites performed. A son, Indula, is born, and two months later he is on earth. Yogasimha stays seven nights and goes home. Out of love for the son, he carries off the boy by his magic. The moon takes the nectar-house in his own body. When the child is lost, Goddess Svarnavati and Ahlada with his family fast and control their senses. The goddess is pleased and a voice without a body says that the child will stay on earth as long as Ahlada stays. Hearing the goddess, they lose their grief.

07-015.json.summary: Suta says that after reciting the Saptashati at the three twilights with love and devotion, a Brahmin's son named Chamunda, Samanta's boy, is well known. At twelve years, after reading the three-part text, he offers to fill a vessel. Sukhakhani brings honey, flowers and fruit, and Devaki offers sacrifice and sandal. Ahlada with his whole body and Udaya with his head bow. The goddess, loving to her devotees, speaks. Balakhani, a great hero, will die after a long time. Devaki will be a goddess and go to her world. Devasimha, free of desire, who died, will reach liberation.

07-016.json.summary: Suta tells of a king of the Shardula line who held a bride-choosing ceremony. Taraka, seeing Balakhani attacked on all sides, has the fierce men bind and beat him. At the king's command, Gajasena, a fire-worshipper, writes. Gajamukta comes. Ahlada with seven hundred thousand men arrives. Seeing the king faint, a man bright as the sun comes. At the goddess's words, Indula, by Indra's command, drives Balakhani out and then Talana. When ten thousand are killed, Krishna's part sends the horse Bindula. When Ahlada reaches home, the wise King Parimala is told.

07-017.json.summary: Suta tells of Vardhana, part of Chitrabana, and Vela. A voice says that whoever will bathe the speaker with streams of blood in the hall will win. Hearing it, Taraka goes quickly with his troops. Netrasimha comes with a hundred thousand troops. A group goes by a fine airplane with fishermen. A man brings divine ornaments from Kubera. Seeing the king's army broken, the angry king takes the palanquin himself and reaches the camp. Someone says the strong Lakshana is the son of Pradyota, and that the king's daughter-in-law Vela is twelve years old. Both took me in fear after defeating me.

07-018.json.summary: Suta describes Mahavati as the ocean among cities and tanks. A lovely woman with all ornaments is seen. King Aryasimha lives in lovely Simhala (Sri Lanka). A woman sees a handsome man in the form of a swan. A great sorrow comes to Ahlada, who wants victory. Hearing the fearful news, the family weeps. Kings, village heads and rulers on the road worship Shiva Rameshvara, set up by Rama. Hearing the letter's words, the stronger king acts. On a day Sukhasharma with three hundred thousand troops comes. For six months the two armies fight.

07-019.json.summary: Suta says the strong Balakhani leaves half of his army and goes with Talana. He visits Aryasimha's house and asks about the cause of everything. A request is made: "give me a vision at once and accept this lovely woman today." When Indula faints, a divine mare appears. By the power of yoga, that weapon is destroyed again. A hero, Indra's son, is wearied. The child, learning of his family, weeps again out of love. After a month on the frightening road, a person dies of wasting disease and goes to heaven.

07-020.json.summary: Suta says that the commander Skanda, born from fire, is pleased and is asked to be gracious, as the bearer of Guha's spear. Lahara, his brother, makes effort for twenty years to bind the demons and to win victory for the gods. A girl named Madanamanjari is born. King Parimala hears of the wise Devasimha. A rogue king speaks to him. He sets up an army of four kinds. The heroes are defeated, a few left alive and terrified. When the army became like water, the stronger Jayanta came. Suta says this is the holy account of Krishna's part.

07-021.json.summary: A sage tells of Pushpa who goes to gather flowers, and of Makaranda, a king's favourite, who turns twelve. A goddess, destroyer of Dhumralochana and Chanda and Munda, is addressed. A friend asks Mahamaya to tell the truth. Pushpavati, who keeps duty, answers: she has seen a beautiful young woman fit for Makaranda, the daughter of a king of the moon-and-sun line. Hearing the harsh news, King Makaranda gathers forty thousand brave camel guards. He binds those proud in war, and gives the daughter by rule with much wealth.

07-022.json.summary: A narrator speaks when Krishna's strong part arrives at Mahavati. She says she worships the Shalagrama stone daily. Sages, gods and ancestors are mentioned. Kali begged the god, her lord, for his own purposes. The strong Udaya, learning the cause of the weeping, eats a rich meal with the Yadavas. The strong Mahiraja besieges the city. Men are blocked and stay in Shirisha town. A man seizes him by the arms to bind him. Virasena binds him, frees the sons and the bride, and the frightened king takes refuge with him. This is Krishna's part's account.

07-023.json.summary: Suta tells of a wicked king who hears a man's weeping. Devasimha gives them much wealth. After the god speaks and vanishes, the king is amazed. A magic spell is stopped and fails. Suryavarma goes home honoured by Makaranda. Talana arrives with a hundred thousand troops. A tremendous battle follows. Eight great warriors are bound by Keshari, the actress. The goddess Pushpavati kills Keshari in anger. The heroes, deluded by her, take refuge. All the kings, honoured by Ahlada, go home.

07-024.json.summary: Suta tells how a messenger reaches the king at Mahavati. When Krishna's part is twenty-five and absorbed in yoga, an arrow, driven by a Vishnu mantra, fails. The strong Lakshana goes to Pundra with Talana and seven hundred thousand troops. Krishna and others take a form of yoga. He comes to Kosala and defeats its king. A father tells the son always to do the king's work. A great battle destroys both armies. A man takes female dress, afraid of the sin of killing a Brahmin. Mahiraja hears of it and turns to Shiva, lord of Uma.

07-025.json.summary: Suta tells what happened when Krishna's part was twenty-six. After ten months a girl with all good qualities is born. She sees all the kings and approaches Lakshana. Talana on a lioness takes up an iron club happily. Sharadanandana goes to the village of Dehli. By the goddess's boon, Devasimha at night meets him. A king bows to them. Sukhakhani aims a fire weapon to calm him. After conquering heroes and crossing twelve pits, the hero falls with a pigeon, deluded by fate. The king burns the empty city to ashes.

07-026.json.summary: Suta says Mahiraja rises, tying his waist in haste. Talana, part of Bhimasena, is a generous commander. Rupana goes on horseback to Saradana. Hearing her words, the king is ashamed. His brother Balakhani, who consorts with ghosts, is addressed. His faithful daughter hears it. Mahiraja is quarrelsome and has a great army. When he faints, they are freed gladly. The strong Saradana kills Madana, born as a cowherd. Ranajit cuts an arrow and the enemy's bow. Mahiraja with eight hundred thousand men comes up.

07-027.json.summary: Suta and the sages speak. A great battle occurs between the leader of people and the king. The king says, "you are my Kshatriya, who gives livelihood to a Brahmin; otherwise Krishna's part will destroy you with your city." Jayachandra, hearing it, comes with troops to the lovely Vetravati river. Lakshana quickly shoots the enemy with a spear. The king is filled with joy. The goddess, the giver of boons, is pleased at the hymn. He had the Gaya ancestor rite done for Balakhani.

07-028.json.summary: Suta tells of the question about who composed the eighteen Puranas and what they give. The wise say six Puranas are of the dark quality, devoted to the duty of Shakti. A courtesan, grieved, takes her best ornaments and speaks fearlessly. He reaches the good city of Sarattana in Bahlika. Someone tells a woman, "listen". The chapter says the sounds born after five months cause worldly existence. She takes the form of a hawk and tries to leave. Indula and Ahlada are woken by Vishnu's illusion. Svarnavati, the goddess Kamakshi, meditates. The war lasted four months.

07-029.json.summary: The sages ask, and Suta tells that a woman, hearing good words, answers in a soft voice. The sage says to Shankara, "salutation to the god of gods". King Bauddhasimha, with seven hundred thousand, is very strong. Indula sits on the fierce horse and a local ruler on an elephant. They arrive at the river Huha. Seven hundred thousand Buddhists are killed and two hundred thousand from the Aryan land. Two hundred thousand more are lost, protected by Krishna's part. Five thousand die struck by Yogasimha's arrows. Ten thousand kings are bound. The eight strong men are sent to march.

07-030.json.summary: Suta tells of the strong Talana, who makes Mahiraja faint and kills five hundred. A man carries grain, a bronze vessel and a vina. The king raises his arm and speaks. Someone comes to Mahiraja and says, "listen". A lovely boon was given, a power of disappearing. Hearing this, Krishna's part goes with his troops. A good courtesan takes a yogic body. A being says Kalagni Rudra set him in a pit in the earth. After gaining a share of Nakula, he enjoys with him great happiness. A great battle of both armies occurs. Suta ends by saying this is the holy account of Krishna's part.

07-031.json.summary: Suta tells of the angry king and Malana. A woman says, "you have freed husbands whom my relative killed." After Varmadeva's view is given, the king, driven by pride, acts. The king's daughter chooses Sukhakhani. On the full moon, a man dear to Chitraratha arrives. Suvela asks her father for a serpent ornament. Ahlada on horseback gives to Mahiraja. Krishna's part, pleased, speaks without fear. The strong Brahmananda faints and falls to the ground. A man says that after killing Taraka, he will come to him.

07-032.json.summary: Suta tells a long battle account. He names warriors such as Durmada, Durvigaha, Nanda and Vikatanana. Mankana comes with ten thousand Kinnaras. Bhagadatta, son of Krishnakumara, arrives. The god fights well with Bhagadatta. When the king of Anga is killed, his ten sons, parts of the Kauravas, go to fight him. Unseen, with harsh arrows, someone roars terribly. The king, afraid, runs quickly to Raktabija. Kalivarma with ten thousand wakes toward Kalinga. Raktabija and Chamunda, strong part of Rama, are named. Kings of the fire line, strong in austerity, appear. A foreigner takes Vidyunmala and much wealth.

08-001.json.summary: This chapter begins the Pratisarga's fourth part. Vedavyasa says that the sub-Puranas will exist in the Kali age. Suta tells of King Ashoka, a Buddhist, who is killed. King Gandharvasena is a strong son of a divine messenger. His son Havirhotra reigns like his father. A boon is given to him. Shambhudatta's son was Bindupala, then Rangapala. The chapter says that on seeing a holy land empty, all live as merchants and are like foreigners on earth.

08-002.json.summary: Suta continues the list of kings. Tomara reigned ten years and his son Mahadeva seven. One ruled half his father's time in the middle land, and then Chandragupta, Nagavaha, Vasanta and Vishala follow, each reigning as his father did. Ananda Deva is born, a handsome son. The son of Anangapala, Kirtimalini, is the eldest. One goes to heaven after casting shade on the Chauhan family. The chapter says that the Mehanas are a foreign people, and the Jatts are Aryan.

08-003.json.summary: Suta tells that after a hundred years the sun, pleased, comes. He calls his son Shukla, an ascetic and best of Brahmins. In the western land of Bharata he ruled for ten years. After conquering the Pulindas and Yavanas he made a country there. He built a city for duty. A girl, an image of a goddess, was playing a flute. The chapter names the river Isha in the west and a bird Markana in the east. A woman alone is distressed. Kumbhapala reigned for half his father's time. Jayachandra and Ratnabhanu rule the east and north, and the others are small kings of mixed castes.

08-004.json.summary: Suta lists the kings: Gauravarman, son of one who reigned like his father; King Shaka, who made a great festival for Mahalakshmi and Mahakali; Katyayana, Vindhyavarman, Keshava and others. The Ganga calls a wise Vidyadhara. Gangadeva reigned ten years. Dhritivarman is his son. Twenty years of rule follow with Sahoddina. The last verse says the family destroys all sin as the moon and sun do.

08-005.json.summary: Suta says the seven continents and oceans became water. Brahma with his arms made the strong king of warriors. Brahmins were born from the moon and kings from the sun. Vishnu was born from the first half and Vamana from the other half. In the Kali age the world-form Hari himself died. In the Satya age he is white, named Hamsa. The god, pleased, says kind words to the gods. He says he was begged by Radha at the end of the Kali age. Those who are devotees of Vishnu know the all-pervading. The chapter ends with salutations to Mahakali, the illusion of Vishnu.

08-006.json.summary: A sage says that from today, in this country, after a hundred years, everything will go. By ignorance my knowledge is withdrawn. The sixteen-part eternal, smaller than the small, is named. The Bhavishya kalpa and the Garuda kalpa are mentioned. He gives the number of human years: nineteen thousand and one lakh. After that, they reached the body of being, consciousness and bliss. Suta is praised there, with eternal yogic sleep. All Vedas and many books were therefore given. The god says that all the stones from Shaladesha will be lost to him. Those who break Vedic duty try to destroy me. Brihaspati then comes and tells the great glory of the sun.

08-007.json.summary: The sages ask, and a story follows. A person pleased the god with fire offerings for a year. A Brahmin tormented by disease went to Shankara, benefactor of the world. A dark deluding mind is told of, whose lord is Shiva. After speaking, the sun produces light from his own mouth. Mitrasharma obtains the daughter of Kamasena. The two choose Mitrasharma and ask for his daughter. He is son of the Kanyakubja Brahmin Devala. By the power of that jewel, a measure of gold is made. A land of Telugu, lovely and visited by divine sages, is named. At a fine and auspicious time, he speaks lovely words and honours the person with "well done".

08-008.json.summary: Brihaspati speaks of making the unwilling friendly with sweet words. King Shantanu is devoted to the sun's vow. A lovely garden is offered to someone. A Brahmin is told that Hari himself is in the form of time. The account of how Vishnusvami came to be is told. Someone is brought back to life and shown, and those who see are amazed. A Brahmin may live a hundred years, wise and free of disease. Nandi's vehicle form is described as a bull. A trader finds that no item in the market is unbought. At a son's birth wealth is gained. The Vedanga, the course of the stars, was destroyed by foreigners.

08-009.json.summary: Suta says that after Jiva (Brihaspati) told the greatness of the sun, someone takes her clothes and speaks fearlessly. Narada's good form, made by Shiva, is mentioned. The sun comes to Kashi. A Brahmin gives up accepting gifts and takes up a craftsman's work. Becoming a Brahmin of a thousand years, the sun himself gives up life. He takes a five-year-old body and is devoted to his father and mother. A Brahmin quickly sees one who is full of detachment. Once the wily Kali, who lives in the heart of thieves' acts, appears. A king, initiated by him, builds a rest-house. Poison is mixed in food by a hypocrite. Suta ends with how Jayadeva came to be.

08-010.json.summary: Jiva (Brihaspati) speaks. A faithful wife, afraid of her husband, hears frightening words. A man says he often got a touchstone out of greed. Two, joined together, are tormented by the fire of Vishnu. A voice says "by you as a swan truth is to be kept, and by you as sacrifice the Veda protected". Marichi and others laugh and ask why he is ready to kill. The name Rama is to be known as destroying all sins. The eternal Lord, a hunter of deer, still stands. Daksha, the Prajapati who burns the worlds by his acts, tormented the gods, sages and ancestors. The chapter ends with the tripundra mark, the rosary and the five-syllable mantra.
